revisions.factsMd:
Mission: find a hosting/serving method that beats vLLM-like engines on **cost per token** (not just latency).
Constraints: no GPU in this swarm environment; workers must reason from papers, public benchmarks, and CPU-scale prototypes — label all numeric claims as estimates.
No repository: durable outputs go to artifacts + board findings; prototype design only until build phase approved.
vLLM baseline stack: PagedAttention KV cache, continuous batching, CUDA kernels, optional speculative decoding plugins — cost drivers are GPU $/hr, memory bandwidth, batch utilization, and tail latency under load.
Finish gates: report artifact, ≥4 critiqued hypotheses, verifier pass.
revisions.guessesMd:
Largest cost wins likely combine: (1) cheaper memory tier for KV (CPU/disk/compression) with acceptable latency tradeoffs; (2) disaggregated prefill vs decode to right-size hardware; (3) aggressive batching + request scheduling for utilization; (4) speculative/cascade paths that cut effective forward passes per token.
Pure software on same GPU fleet may yield <2× cost; structural changes (disaggregation, heterogeneous tiers, spot/preemptible orchestration) may reach 2–5× on specific workloads.
CPU-only serving is unlikely to beat GPU vLLM on $/token for 7B+ at production QPS — but hybrid or small-model edge paths might for narrow SLAs.
revisions.planMd:
Phase A (cycles 1–N): parallel surveys → each researcher proposes 1–2 hypotheses with evidence URLs → critic challenges → ranker runs Elo tournament on cost-per-token potential.
Phase B: promote top 2 hypotheses → deep dive tasks → synthesizer draft report with ranked recommendation + prototype architecture.
Phase C: verifier checks claims/sources → orchestrator declare_done OR request_phase_change if coded prototype warranted.
Worker team now: 3 researchers (KV/memory, disaggregation, batching+speculative) + 1 critic; add ranker when ≥3 hypotheses; add synthesizer when leaderboard stabilizes.

Is beating vLLM on **identical hardware** required, or any cloud topology allowed?
